metadata.title: Five-year comparable fiscal framework 2026–2030
metadata.status: Official baseline populated. Party-specific annual balances are not calculated where comparable year-by-year costing data are absent.
metadata.scope: Transparent baseline and sensitivity model; not a full independent forecast.

sources.name: PBO — 2024 manifesto tax and welfare modelling

limitations: Gross voted expenditure is not total general-government expenditure and must not be subtracted from tax revenue to recreate the general-government balance.
PBO reports 2030 endpoint percentage deviations for selected tax and welfare measures only; these cannot be projected linearly across earlier years or converted to euros without baseline totals.
Corporation-tax windfall estimates are uncertain and not guaranteed recurring revenue.
Party manifesto costings use inconsistent periods, baselines and classifications; missing values remain uncosted rather than imputed.

parties.known: Party manifesto stated a €3bn net tax package over five years (2024-era analysis); whole programme annual cost schedule not available in a common format.

Party manifesto states €31.2bn spending increase 2026–2030, €14.1bn additional capital expenditure from Apple receipts, €6bn tax revenue attributed to wage growth and €1.1bn revenue-raising measures. Party claims require reconciliation.
missing: Timing and eligibility of Apple-funded capital

parties.known: Manifesto provides housing tenure targets; PBO models selected tax/welfare measures only. Whole-programme annual balance not independently established.
missing: Annual current and capital cost by programme
Annual tax measures and corporation-tax assumptions

parties.known: Manifesto states additional €2.8bn capital allocation per year by 2029 for housing and around €1bn annual capital for affordable/cost-rental measures; overlap needs checking.

Manifesto reports €12.063bn average additional spending per year 2026–2030, including housing €3.980bn, health €3.300bn, disability €1.054bn, education €749m, welfare €1.415bn, climate/nature €540m, childcare €505m and other €520m. Party-stated estimates.
PBO covers selected tax/welfare policies only; manifesto climate, retrofit, transport and public-service capital investment not independently costed in that model.
missing: Project-level capital costs and annual cash profiles

parties.known: PBO covers selected tax/welfare policies only; public construction and expanded public provision require additional capital and workforce costing.
missing: State construction-company set-up and operating costs

parties.known: Several measure-specific party estimates exist; no comparable PBO result in the seven-party report.
Manifesto gives selected set-up/operating costs and a 10% public-spending savings ambition; savings yield is not verified.

rules: Illustrative adjusted balance = published general-government balance − (estimated excess corporation tax × haircut).
This holds all other factors constant; it is not a forecast and does not model macroeconomic or behavioural responses.
No party-specific annual balance is calculated until comparable annual current spending, capital spending, tax changes, savings and funding schedules are available.
conclusion: The official baseline projects a €6.725bn general-government surplus in 2026, narrowing to €0.935bn in 2029 before rising to €5.730bn in 2030. Estimated excess corporation-tax receipts range from €18.8bn to €26.0bn annually. Removing that entire estimated component, with everything else unchanged, would turn each projected surplus into a deficit. This is a one-factor sensitivity, not a forecast. Current manifesto data do not support nine comparable annual party balances: annual cost, revenue and timing schedules are inconsistent or absent. The model therefore displays the official baseline, stress tests, PBO's comparable 2030 endpoint and missing party inputs rather than inventing totals.
